9. import torch.nn.functional as functional

15. 
16. 
17. def no_autocast(device_type: str):
18.     if device_type in {"cpu", "cuda"}:
19.         return torch.autocast(device_type=device_type, enabled=False)
20.     return contextlib.nullcontext()
21. 
22. 
23. class LoRALinear(nn.Module):
24.     def __init__(self, base: nn.Linear, rank: int, alpha: float):
25.         super().__init__()
26.         self.base_layer = base
27.         self.scale = alpha / rank
28.         initial_A = torch.empty(
29.             rank, base.in_features, dtype=torch.float32, device="cpu"
30.         )
31.         nn.init.kaiming_uniform_(initial_A, a=math.sqrt(5))
32.         self.lora_A = nn.Parameter(
33.             initial_A.to(device=base.weight.device)
34.         )
35.         self.lora_B = nn.Parameter(
36.             torch.zeros(
37.                 base.out_features,
38.                 rank,
39.                 dtype=torch.float32,
40.                 device=base.weight.device,
41.             )
42.         )
43. 
44.     @property
45.     def weight(self) -> torch.Tensor:
46.         return self.base_layer.weight
47. 
48.     @property
49.     def bias(self) -> torch.Tensor | None:
50.         return self.base_layer.bias
51. 
52.     def forward(self, inputs: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
53.         base = self.base_layer(inputs)
54.         with no_autocast(inputs.device.type):
55.             update = functional.linear(
56.                 functional.linear(inputs.float(), self.lora_A),
57.                 self.lora_B,
58.             )
59.         return base + update.to(base.dtype) * self.scale
60.

62. def attach_adapter(model: Any) -> Any:
63.     for parameter in model.parameters():
64.         parameter.requires_grad_(False)
65.     layers = getattr(getattr(model, "model", None), "layers", None)
66.     if not isinstance(layers, nn.ModuleList):
67.         raise RuntimeError("model does not expose decoder layers")
68.     for layer in layers:
69.         attention = getattr(layer, "self_attn", None)
70.         if attention is None:
71.             raise RuntimeError("decoder layer has no self attention")
72.         for name in ADAPTER_TARGETS:
73.             base = getattr(attention, name, None)
74.             if not isinstance(base, nn.Linear):
75.                 raise RuntimeError(f"{name} is not linear")
76.             setattr(
77.                 attention,
78.                 name,
79.                 LoRALinear(base, ADAPTER_RANK, ADAPTER_ALPHA),
80.             )
81.     return model
82. 
83. 
84. def adapter_parameters(model: Any) -> dict[str, nn.Parameter]:
85.     values = {
86.         name: parameter
87.         for name, parameter in model.named_parameters()
88.         if name.endswith(".lora_A") or name.endswith(".lora_B")
89.     }
90.     if not values:
91.         raise RuntimeError("adapter has no parameters")
92.     return values
93. 
94. 
95. def save_adapter(model: Any, output_dir: Path) -> None:
96.     output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
97.     save_file(
98.         {
99.             name: parameter.detach().cpu().contiguous()
100.             for name, parameter in adapter_parameters(model).items()
101.         },
102.         output_dir / "adapter.safetensors",
103.     )
104.     write_json(
105.         output_dir / "adapter_config.json",
106.         {
107.             "adapter_type": "attention_lora",
108.             "alpha": ADAPTER_ALPHA,
109.             "rank": ADAPTER_RANK,
110.             "target_modules": list(ADAPTER_TARGETS),
111.         },
112.         exclusive=True,
113.     )
114.

116. def load_adapter(model: Any, output_dir: Path) -> None:
117.     config = read_json(output_dir / "adapter_config.json")
118.     if (
119.         config.get("adapter_type") != "attention_lora"
120.         or int(config["rank"]) != ADAPTER_RANK
121.         or float(config["alpha"]) != ADAPTER_ALPHA
122.         or tuple(config["target_modules"]) != ADAPTER_TARGETS
123.     ):
124.         raise RuntimeError("adapter configuration differs")
125.     attach_adapter(model)
126.     parameters = adapter_parameters(model)

757. def find_packed_sequence_indices(position_ids: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor | None:
758.     """
759.     Find the indices of the sequence to which each new query token in the sequence belongs when using packed
760.     tensor format (i.e. several sequences packed in the same batch dimension).
761. 
762.     Args:
763.         position_ids (`torch.Tensor`)
764.             A 2D tensor of shape (batch_size, query_length) indicating the positions of each token in the sequences.
765. 
766.     Returns:
767.         A 2D tensor where each similar integer indicates that the tokens belong to the same sequence. For example, if we
768.         pack 3 sequences of 2, 3 and 1 tokens respectively along a single batch dim, this will return [[0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 2]].
769. 
770.         If the there is only one sequence in each batch item (and we don't compile), then we return `None` indicating
771.         no packed sequences. This is the same as [[0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]] for the example above.
772.     """
773.     # What separate different sequences is when 2 consecutive positions_ids are separated by more than 1. So
774.     # taking the diff (by prepending the first value - 1 to keep correct indexing) and applying cumsum to the result
775.     # gives exactly the sequence indices
776.     # Note that we assume that a single sequence cannot span several batch dimensions, i.e. 1 single sequence
777.     # cannot be part of the end of the first batch dim and the start of the 2nd one for example
778.     first_dummy_value = position_ids[:, :1] - 1  # We just need the diff on this first value to be 1
779.     position_diff = torch.diff(position_ids, prepend=first_dummy_value, dim=-1)
780.     packed_sequence_mask = (position_diff != 1).cumsum(-1)
781. 
782.     # Sadly this is a dynamic control flow, so we cannot enable this check on anything compile related
783.     if not is_tracing(packed_sequence_mask) and (packed_sequence_mask[:, -1] == 0).all():
784.         return None
785. 
786.     return packed_sequence_mask
787.

790.     config: PreTrainedConfig,
791.     inputs_embeds: torch.Tensor,
792.     attention_mask: torch.Tensor | BlockMask | None,
793.     past_key_values: Cache | None,
794.     position_ids: torch.Tensor | None,
795.     layer_idx: int | None,
796.     encoder_hidden_states: torch.Tensor | None = None,
797. ) -> tuple[bool, torch.Tensor | BlockMask | None, int, int]:
798.     """
799.     Perform some common pre-processing of the mask arguments we get from the modeling code. Mostly determine the
800.     key-value length and offsets, and if we should early exit or not.
801. 
802.     Args:
803.         config (`PreTrainedConfig`):
804.             The model config.
805.         inputs_embeds (`torch.Tensor`):
806.             The input embeddings of shape (batch_size, query_length, hidden_dim). This is used only to infer the
807.             batch size, query length and dtype.
808.         attention_mask (`torch.Tensor`, optional):
809.             The 2D attention mask corresponding to padded tokens of shape (batch_size, number_of_seen_tokens+q_length).
810.             It can also be an already prepared 4D mask, in which case it is returned as-is.
811.         past_key_values (`Cache`, optional):

818.         encoder_hidden_states (`torch.Tensor`, optional):

820.             `inputs_embeds` to infer the kv length.
821.

This is the complete, verified fix. Summary of findings:

**Bug found:** In `source/collator.py`, `PackedBatchCollator` packed multiple documents into one sequence, correctly resetting `position_ids` per document, but also set `attention_mask = torch.ones_like(input_ids)`. I traced `transformers`' `masking_utils.py` (v5.12.1) and confirmed: automatic packed-sequence block-diagonal masking only activates when `attention_mask is None` and `position_ids` resets are present. Passing a dense all-ones mask defeats that detection, so the causal mask falls back to a single full causal mask spanning the whole pack — documents leak attention into each other.

I verified this empirically two ways:
1. Direct introspection of `_preprocess_mask_arguments`/`find_packed_sequence_indices` showing `packed_sequence_mask` is `None` when `attention_mask` is all-ones, but correctly block-diagonal when `attention_mask=None`.
2. Using the actual `collator.py`+`model.py` code on real training data: perturbing document 0's tokens changed document 3's logits by **5.6** max-diff with the buggy mask, vs **exactly 0.0** with the fix — proof of leakage and proof of correction.

Fixed by removing the `attention_mask` key from the collator output so `training.py`'s `if name in batch` filter naturally omits it, letting the library auto-detect packing from `position_ids`. Verified end-to-end forward/backward on CPU: finite loss and gradients, matching original loss scale.
